title: A second worktree
brief:
Production needs a hotfix branch right now, but your main checkout is full of half-done rework. Switching means stash gymnastics; cloning again means waiting. Real git has a third door: `git worktree add` checks out a SECOND working directory from the same repository, with its own branch, sharing the one object store.

Create one: `git worktree add -b hotfix hotfix-dir` makes the branch `hotfix` and checks it out in `hotfix-dir`, while your dirty main stays exactly as it is. Confirm with `git worktree list`.

One rule explains the design: a branch can be checked out in only one worktree at a time. Try `git switch hotfix` afterwards (not part of the solution) and read the refusal.
hints: git worktree list shows both checkouts: main here, hotfix in hotfix-dir.
The branch-exclusivity rule is the lesson: the worktree OWNS hotfix until you git worktree remove it.
